text:
Liz H: Heads-up — I ran a microprofile this morning on the continuous batcher with the new token-budget heuristic. saw a consistent latency spike for short "cache-hit" requests when we applied virtual-length=1 for hits. :eyes:
Mario C: curious — do you mean those ~5–20 token tail requests?
Liz H: yep. 50th/95th jumped ~8–12ms on p50 and ~20ms on p95 for small seqs on A100 pool.
Sara P: can you paste the profile output? I want to see kernel selection counts.
Liz H: pasted below (trimmed):
```
profile: run=2026-03-16T07:12Z
requests: 10k sample
- cache-hit (virtual_len=1): conv-kernel calls 18k, attn-kernel fastpath 6.2k
- cache-miss (real_len=60): conv-kernel calls 9k, attn-kernel mixed 15k
cpu/gpu overlap  -> lower for hit-path
```
Mario C: interesting — more conv-kernel calls on hits? that suggests we’re breaking microbatch packing in a way that increases kernel-switch overhead.
Ryan M: could be because virtual_len=1 exposes many single-token microbatches that can't be coalesced by the prefetch window.
Liz H: exact hunch. The packer is currently honoring virtual_length for admission but not collapsing adjacent hit requests when they’re separated by cache-prefetch markers.
Sara P: do we have the admission/queue policy config used?
Liz H: config used: 
```
batcher: {
  max_tokens: 1024,
  token_budget: dynamic,  # token_budget targets adaptive to latency
  virtual_length_for_cache_hits: 1,
  prefetch_window_ms: 4,
  max_microbatch_size: 32
}
```
Mario C: two quick experiments: (A) raise virtual_length_for_cache_hits to 4, (B) keep vlen=1 but add a collapsing pass that merges consecutive hit microbatches within prefetch_window. Which do we try first?
Ryan M: try collapsing pass first — cheaper change and keeps unit-cost accounting intact.
Liz H: agreed. implemented a prototype collapsing pass that merges hit requests if they arrive within prefetch_window and target kernel is identical. It reduced conv-kernel calls by ~30% in the sample run.
perf-bot: regression alert cleared for canary 2312467001 (after collapse-probe) :white_check_mark:
Mario C: nice. any impact on latency numbers?
Liz H: p50 improved back to baseline, p95 reduced ~10ms from the earlier spike, throughput unchanged. We did see a small increase in median kernel runtime because merged microbatches sometimes switch to the mixed-attn kernel, but overall end-to-end was better.
Sara P: what about fairness — do long prefix-miss requests get starved?
Liz H: no starvation seen in 1 hour test. collapsing only affects hit-only contiguous sets and respects max_microbatch_size. admission still prioritizes oldest requests first.
Ryan M: two follow-ups: (1) add kernel-selection telemetry to the trace so we can see when merge triggers kernel fallback, (2) try a token-budget heuristic that gives hits a slightly higher token_budget_target to encourage merges.
Mario C: for (2) propose: token_budget_target = base_target * (1 + 0.2 * is_prefix_hit). That nudges packer to prefer merging hits.
Liz H: I simulated Mario's formula. merge rate up 12%, p95 improved another ~3ms, but cost-per-token slightly increased ~0.6% because larger mixed kernels are slightly more expensive on some models.
Sara P: tradeoff seems acceptable for production defaults. We should gate via a rollout flag and add perf regression alert thresholds.
Liz H: plan: canary the collapsing-pass + token_budget tweak behind flag "hit-collapse-v1" for 72h on a subset of A100 nodes. Collect: kernel-selection counts, end-to-end p50/p95, cost-per-token. I'll create the canary and PR.
Ryan M: add a trace label when collapse merges >1 microbatch so we can query easily.
Mario C: I'll draft the PR description and add the chart queries.
Liz H: thanks — assigning follow-ups: @Mario C (PR + queries), @Ryan M (trace label), @Sara P (regression thresholds). I'll kick off canary in ~30m. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: new canary started: hit-collapse-v1 on pool-a100-canary (id=cc-2312468)
Sara P: FYI — also double-check kernel selector heuristics; merged hits sometimes trigger fallback to float16 path on older nodes which increases mem-bandwidth. If that happens, we may want a node-aware token_budget multiplier.
Liz H: noted. will add a node-tagged metric.
Mario C: LGTM. thanks everyone.
Liz H: closing thread once canary completes, will post summary.
